title: Symmetric Mass Generation for Domain-Wall Fermions
authors: Sho Araki, Hidenori Fukaya, Tetsuya Onogi, Satoshi Yamaguchi
abstract: We report the first numerical examination of symmetric mass generation (SMG) for domain-wall fermions. Our simulation on a two-dimensional Euclidean lattice computes the path-integral of the Fidkowski-Kitaev Majorana chain with two boundaries, corresponding to the two (physical and mirror) walls. We demonstrate by evaluating the lattice Dirac operator eigenvalue spectrum that the local four-Fermi interaction selectively gaps the edge fermions on the mirror wall while leaving the physical wall intact. We further identify a characteristic signature of SMG in the path-integral: the gap of the Dirac operator opens along the imaginary axis of the complex spectrum, in contrast to the standard mass shift in the real direction. The conventional hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm remains practical with reweighting the complex phase of the Pfaffian, which is found to be remarkably small throughout the simulation. These results provide a practical nonperturbative framework for interaction-induced mirror-fermion decoupling of lattice domain-wall fermions.
summary: This work numerically examines Symmetric Mass Generation (SMG) in domain-wall fermions, a model used in lattice gauge theory. By simulating the system with a four-Fermi interaction, the authors show that the interaction selectively gaps the 'mirror' fermion mode while preserving the physical mode. This provides a practical, nonperturbative method for decoupling unwanted mirror fermions.
main_problem: The paper investigates Symmetric Mass Generation (SMG) for domain-wall fermions, specifically addressing the 'mirror-fermion problem' in lattice gauge theory.
main_result: The simulation demonstrates that the local four-Fermi interaction can selectively gap the edge fermions on the mirror wall while leaving the physical wall intact, confirming a nonperturbative framework for decoupling.
method: The study employs numerical simulation using the Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithm to analyze the eigenvalue spectrum of the lattice Dirac operator.
model_or_system: The system models domain-wall fermions using the Euclidean path integral of the Fidkowski-Kitaev Majorana chain on a two-dimensional lattice, incorporating a four-Fermi interaction term.
key_observables: The gap opening in the Dirac operator eigenvalue spectrum, the location of the gap opening (imaginary axis vs. real mass shift), and the scaling of the generated gap with lattice size.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($g_2^P$), bare mass ($m$), and lattice size ($L_t/a$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the reflection symmetry ($R_t$) is exact in the lattice formulation, and the HMC algorithm remains practical due to small Pfaffian phase fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the eigenvalue spectrum showing gap opening in the imaginary direction for $g_2^P > 0$ (Fig. 1), and plot the spectrum confirming the $(L_t/a)^2$ scaling of the gap on the mirror wall (Fig. 2).
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism for the action, analyzes the eigenvalue spectrum for both chiral (no domain walls) and reflection (two domain walls) scenarios, and concludes by establishing the nonperturbative mechanism for mirror-fermion decoupling.
why_interesting: While focused on lattice gauge theory, the study of interaction-induced gap opening and spectral properties in fermionic systems is relevant to understanding emergent mass gaps in strongly correlated electron models.
